transcript.text: Green Valley Garden Centre, Ruth Elliot speaking.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: Hello, my name's Mark Taylor. I'm calling about the job advertised on your website.
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Ah yes. The sales assistant position. Have you read the description?
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: I have, but I wanted to check a few details. Is the job at your main shop on Kingsway?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Yes, that's right, the one on Kingsway. We also have a smaller branch in the village, but the vacancy is here.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: How many hours a week would it be?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Twenty hours, spread over four days. We prefer to have the same people every week, so that customers see familiar faces.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: Four days a week is fine. I'm studying part-time, so I'd like to keep one day free for lectures.
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: That should be possible. We ask staff to tell us their university days at the beginning of the year.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: And what is the pay?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: It's eleven pounds fifty an hour, and after six months it goes up to twelve pounds. You also get a staff discount of twenty percent on plants.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: That sounds good. When would the job start?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: We would like someone to start on the first Monday of September. That gives us time to train the person before the autumn rush.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: September is perfect. That gives me a month to finish my current job.
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: We train new staff in the first two weeks, so you'll have a lot of support.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: Do I need any particular experience?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Previous customer service experience is the main requirement. Knowledge of plants is useful, but we can teach that. What is your background?
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: I've worked in a clothes shop for three years, so I'm used to dealing with customers.
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Retail experience is always welcome here, especially from people who enjoyed it.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: I did. I liked helping people find what they needed.
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: That's excellent. In that case, I'd like to invite you for an interview. It would be a short chat, followed by a trial hour on the shop floor.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: A trial on the shop floor? That's interesting. When would that be?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Next Tuesday at two o'clock, if that suits you. Please bring two references, and a form of identification such as a passport.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: Tuesday at two is fine. Should I wear anything special?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Just wear comfortable shoes, as you'll be standing for most of the time. You don't need to wear a suit.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: I'll be ready. I've always enjoyed gardening, and I have a small vegetable patch at home.
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: That's a good sign. Customers often ask for advice, and personal experience helps a lot.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: Thank you very much. And what's the deadline for applications?
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: The end of this month. But as I said, since you're coming for an interview, you don't need to send anything else.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms Elliot. I'll see you on Tuesday.
transcript.speaker: MARK

transcript.text: Looking forward to it. Goodbye.
transcript.speaker: MS ELLIOT
